bars.says: On the Blue Desert, the player sees blue distance giving way to pale ice and small transparent branching plants up close, interrupted by abandoned workings and wrecks.

meant.intent: Keep the beautiful, apparently empty ancient ice plateau as a place rather than a normal snow map or bioweapon landscape.
meant.source: design/Jawa/worldbuilding/biomes/the_blue_desert.md sections 1, 8, 9; owner experience in design/RimMandrake/biome_experiences_2026-10-20.md. The exact contrasting pictures are delegated from those sources.

figurative.stands_for: The broad local-map expanse reads blue at travel zoom. Top-down zoom supplies the distant view.
figurative.accept: At travel zoom a top-down ice plain reads blue without a horizon or perspective depth.

figurative.stands_for: Translucent branching bodies reveal underlying ice through their centers, with visible refracting edges and highlights.
figurative.accept: A branch has bright refracting edges and a translucent center through which the ice remains visible.

accept: At travel zoom the top-down plateau reads blue and open without a horizon or perspective depth. Closer inspection reveals pale ice through translucent branching plant centers, bright refracting edges and discontinuous traces of abandoned excavation.
Rust, scorch and mineral glints can interrupt the pale scene at an old work site without coloring ordinary ice and plants blue.
reject: A snowy conifer plain or a wall of opaque blue shrubs fills the playable ground.
Only the world icon is blue: the local map is generic white snow with generic plants and unrelated wreck props.
bars.lazy: Only the world icon is blue: the local map is generic white snow with generic plants and unrelated wreck props.

range.left_out: No planetary painting, tile-count criterion, new planet, asset-variant quota, or frame-perfect optical scattering simulation. Workings are physical land content, not the deferred epoch ladder.

bars.says: The player sees deep ice-sand buildup beside walls, doors and hulls heavily slow approach routes until cleared or eroded, while ice fog visibly cuts shooting reach and slows travel until it lifts.

meant.intent: Deep means the thickest SandGrid buildup reaching structure approaches and imposing its heaviest path cost, with routine fog also affecting work and travel.
meant.source: the_blue_desert.md section 4b engine amendment, including owner deep-drift instruction at BLUEDESERT_DESIGN_SITTING_1; numerical severity is a check, not a bar. Haze appearance remains B1; exposure is deferred by this Designer.

figurative.stands_for: The thickest SandGrid buildup reaches approach cells beside a wall, door or hull and applies its heaviest movement cost until cleared or eroded.
figurative.accept: A top-down ice-grain layer reaches the thickest buildup category beside a doorway. Haulers can still cross it, taking longer until a sand-clear area is worked.

figurative.stands_for: Deposits occupy approach cells beside a structure. The structure need not cause or redirect accumulation.
figurative.accept: A patchy deposit fills approach cells beside a wall and slows doorway traffic even though the wall did not redirect wind or cause the patch.

figurative.stands_for: Fog prevents shots that the same weapon can target in clear weather.
figurative.accept: A weapon remains intact but cannot target the same distant enemy until the fog lifts.

accept: A patchy ice-grain deposit reaches its thickest buildup beside a wall, door or hull, heavily slowing haulers across the approach. Working a sand-clear area restores the deposit-free trip, and exposed deposits later erode. The structure need not cause the patch.
A weapon remains intact but loses a previously available distant shot in fog, and a deposit-free trip also slows. Both recover as fog lifts.
reject: Only a dusting or thin layer ever reaches structure approaches.
A storm overlay or storm-time movement penalty slows travel while approach cells retain no buildup.
Weather definitions contain penalties, but the test map stays clear, or fog never releases its restrictions.
bars.lazy: Only a dusting or thin layer ever reaches structure approaches.

bars.says: A crew can clear live growth and keep an escape route before excavating, so warming or damaging connected native fuel can spread an explosive chain while separated work avoids carrying that chain into the crew.

meant.intent: Caution is preparation and containment, not mystical mining speed; the player must be able to make the same site safer without deleting the signature.
meant.source: Owner experience sentence in biome_experiences_2026-10-20.md; later owner answer one in designer_codex_2026-11-09/BlueDesert/ANSWERS_OWNER.md; hydrocarbon explosive-chain lore. Exact containment definition delegated.

figurative.word: carrying that chain into the crew
figurative.stands_for: Successive fuel releases or their heat reach the crew through a causal propagation path.
figurative.accept: The crew carries no burning object, yet blasts along an uncleared plant patch reach its work area.

accept: The crew cuts and hauls living fuel away from its exit and recovery area before mining ordinary water ice; a later ignition consumes a connected patch without jumping the cleared separation into their retreat.

At the same uncleared site a flame or native death starts discrete neighboring blasts that reach the work area although the crew carries no burning object. Sustained warming gives a locatable warning that lets an attentive crew turn heat off and retreat.
reject: An isolated plant explodes but a connected field never propagates, or an ignition crosses empty ice without a causal fuel or heat path.
Mining fewer blocks is called careful, yet clearing and retreat cannot change which crew is caught; the only safe proof has native explosions disabled.
bars.lazy: Mining fewer blocks is called careful, yet clearing and retreat cannot change which crew is caught; the only safe proof has native explosions disabled.

range.left_out: No guaranteed survival while standing in a lethal blast, no immunity from an unrelated raid, no safe ice-mining technique unlock, no standoff-distance stat pinned as a bar. A gap with a live animal/cargo bridge is not separated.

bars.says: Native corpses, wax and feed stay useful when cold and become a warned explosive hazard when warmed, while loose water ice keeps a closed cold room cold without a rack for far longer than an ordinary cooling repair.

meant.intent: Native hazard continuity covers corpses, wax and feed through storage and wax bill work. Loose ice alone must keep a prepared closed cold hold cold, with a substantial reserve beyond ordinary cooling repair time under its declared load.
meant.source: the_blue_desert.md hard ban on warm-safe native organics; owner answer two in ANSWERS_OWNER.md; later ordinary ice-mining answer; blue_desert_hydrocarbon_life.md section 7 explicitly yields ordinary Chemfuel from cold-room refining. Loose-ice heat accounting and warning reset policy are delegated. The ordinary refining rule is R10.

figurative.stands_for: An ordinary repair finishes with substantial ice reserve and continued cold holding remaining under the same declared heat load. Duration is a comparison to ordinary labor.
figurative.accept: A finite stockpile still holds the unpowered room cold well after a matched crew has finished ordinary cooler repair, and eventually melts if heat input continues.

accept: Loose ice alone holds a prepared closed room and its native cargo cold. In an unrepaired blackout arm it continues doing so with substantial reserve well after a matched crew finishes ordinary cooler repair, and eventually melts under continued heat input.

Cold wax, feed and a newly generated native corpse retain their warm hazard through splitting, carrying and reloading. Wax stays reactive during bill work, with a warm workroom ruining or wicking the input before completion. A cold-room bill yields ordinary vanilla Chemfuel. Water ice melts without exploding.
reject: Native organics become warm-safe as a corpse, newborn product, split or merged stack, carried item or processed food, or wax loses its warm reaction while the refinery bill is still in progress.
Only the special rack cools a room, or a warm organic stack goes directly from apparently sound to destruction before the player can locate it and respond.
A full prepared ice stockpile melts away before an ordinary repair crew can finish, or keeps the room cold only until shortly after that repair.
bars.lazy: A full prepared ice stockpile melts away before an ordinary repair crew can finish, or keeps the room cold only until shortly after that repair.

range.varies: All native plants, live heat tolerance, generated corpses, wax, roe, butcher outputs and enabled shared-engine products; fresh/stored/damaged, stack count 1 through loaded stack limit, merge/split, held/spawned, room/landed ship interior/transport container; ambient -60 through +40 C, door traffic 0/ordinary/40-colonist bursts, 1/12/40 colonists, powered cooling/on/off/repaired, loose-ice no/partial/full reserve, room sizes 9/36/144 cells; save/reload at warming/warning/ice-exhaustion/wick boundaries. Off-map containers may preserve a recorded hazard state but may not become free indefinite refrigeration. Sweep wax bill start/progress/completion/cancellation with the ingredient hazard active until completion. Completed output is ordinary vanilla Chemfuel under R10. For the long-duration comparison use full prepared reserves in closed rooms with positive measured heat input and healthy, available ordinary repair workers with reachable materials. Time an actual standard repair of the same cooling fault and route under each admitted weather/load regime. Continue an identical unrepaired arm beyond repair completion to read reserve and cold holding. Partial/empty reserves, open-door bursts and deliberately excessive heat are exhaustion stress cases, not promises of long holding from any quantity of ice.
range.left_out: No physically infinite outdoor refrigerator or arbitrary target-temperature gizmo on loose ice. No new meltwater drip interaction. Plain water ice, potable water, metal and declared pure-carbon char-lace are not hydrocarbon organics. Char-lace production itself is off.

Compare loaded versus empty ice and repaired versus still-unpowered arms. Record the same ordinary cooler fault, repair materials, worker state and access route. Use positive heat input sufficient to warm the empty-ice room.

bars.says: Across a season on a full Blue Desert map, a working colony can repeatedly discover, clear, extract and cold-store resources while weather and native life continue, a local ignition remains understandable, and reloading or reversing the work order causes neither runaway destruction nor a dead or stalled biome.

meant.intent: The complete first version must remain beautiful, alive and usable through its own hazards, without a map-wide chain on routine predation, accumulating chores, disappearing life or an error storm.
meant.source: Whole-bar mandate in this cleanse brief; delegated synthesis of owner experience, ordinary mining/cooling answers and life commission. This is a proposed obligation, not a measured seasonal result.

figurative.stands_for: An ignition starts at an identified work-site fuel source. The player can trace subsequent releases along reachable fuel/heat paths using in-game warnings and event evidence.
figurative.accept: A blast starts beyond the camera and reaches a neighboring patch. On return, the player can identify the warmed wax source and follow the affected fuel path from the in-game evidence.

figurative.stands_for: Routine predation or ordinary work repeatedly propagates releases across the food web until the next expedition loses living resources and usable work sites.
figurative.accept: A careless shot destroys a connected patch. Its chain ends at a cleared separation, and later expeditions still meet native life and usable sites.

figurative.stands_for: Dead means native growth and animals are gone for the next expedition. Stalled means ordinary discovery, clearing, extraction, hauling or cooling repair cannot progress through the season under the declared inputs.
figurative.accept: One patch is bare and fog temporarily delays hauling. Growth and animals persist elsewhere, fog lifts, and workers complete the next extraction and repair.

accept: Wild growth and predation continue between expeditions; a prepared cold hold weathers a repairable blackout, a careless work site suffers a traceable chain, and the next expedition still finds life, routes and work.
After a mid-season reload, workers still finish the alternate haul/clear/excavate sequence, cooling reserves and warnings retain their meaning, and the map remains usable without scripted rescues.
reject: Routine hunting repeatedly detonates the food web until the whole map is bare, or growth refills every cleared separation before crews can use it.

A beautiful proof pad passes only with clear sky or explosions locked off; the full run stalls jobs, floods predators or cargo, loses warning state on reload, silently deletes animals or repeatedly logs errors.
bars.lazy: A beautiful proof pad passes only with clear sky or explosions locked off; the full run stalls jobs, floods predators or cargo, loses warning state on reload, silently deletes animals or repeatedly logs errors.

range.varies: Full 200/250/300-cell local maps; 15-day season with tick order/tick rates unmodified, 1/12/40-colonist colonies, cold ambient traces -60 to -19 C with heated rooms, ordinary and concentrated wild distribution; initial scarcity/ordinary/high local plant and prey availability; natural weather traces including all weather transitions; controlled reachable-site ignition and repairable blackout as challenges in each trace; save on day 7 or 8, reload, then complete remaining season. Reverse sequences clear→mine→haul and haul loose cargo→clear→mine, and reduce traffic→repair versus repair→reduce traffic. Re-run after day-100 baseline for accumulated state. Compression means faster wall-clock speed only, never skipping ticks, jobs, heat, growth, ecology or weather.
range.left_out: No claim of guaranteed recovery from deliberately heating all organics or global hostile bombardment. A crew that carries fuel through its own separation has not met containment preparation. No canonical world writes or alternative planet sweeps. Enjoyment is predicted, not graded.

sees.instrument: Whole-season model first screens recorded geometries; then an instrumented full-map run reads resource provenance, jobs, ecology, blast/heat causal graphs, weather, departure signs and logs. Runtime traces decide state claims; B1 still requires the visual look. T15 adds a full-map observer and exact replay/recovery protocol; no current seasonal instrument is adequate.
sees.start: A working colony with all kept systems, a discoverable site, real native food and prepared cold hold; fingerprint source/defs/assembly/settings/assets/dependencies/save. Record initial states and quotas of neither flora nor animals as bars; log natural events without forcing sky clear. The blackout hold receives measured heat leakage from an adjacent room with a fueled heater that remains running throughout the electrical outage. Record its fuel, heat transfer and room connection in matched ice/no-ice copies, sufficient to warm the no-ice hold beyond the loaded wax safe-temperature limit.
sees.on: Every kept mechanic enabled at proposed shipped defaults: ordinary roster/growth/predation, native and flora charges, foreign-ingestion response, warning cues, weather rotation, departure signs, corpse/product reactivity and loose-ice cooling; next-version extras off. All DLC installed, research unlocked, no weather/time/health locks or invulnerable fixtures. Shared engines retain their declared shipped settings. Challenges are actions in this running state, never a hazard-off substitute.
sees.control: A scripted test can replenish animals, spawn resources or cool rooms between readings. Log every external intervention and reject unexplained additions/removals; paired untreated ecological areas distinguish autonomous ecology. During the same blackout, verify the fueled neighboring heater stays active in both copies. The no-ice hold must warm past the wax safe limit while the ice hold stays below it with measured reserve loss. Match initial temperatures, heater fuel, leakage and door traffic, and record electric cooling as off until repair. Repeat after reload and reversed action order without clearing field state.
sees.reset: Use a disposable saved local map, preserve a baseline save plus settings/weather-lock journal before staging; reload that baseline and reread pawn IDs, items, room temperatures, sand depths, weather freedom and settings after the reading. Do not clear an arbitrary rectangle or restore guessed defaults. No canonical save is touched.
sees.live_only_why: State histories and calibrated offline replay can distinguish the pictured causes; no subjective live judgment is asserted.

tests.reject: Reject this version if false: The complete first version must remain beautiful, alive and usable through its own hazards, without a map-wide chain on routine predation, accumulating chores, disappearing life or an error storm.
tests.renormalize: Pictures compare behavior and visible relationships; retuning yields, dimensions, timings or variant counts does not change their classification.

checks.what: Resolve patched XML roster as named elements; preserve current membership, densities and cold/dark/fertility-independent unsowable flora flags. Assert no removed donor plants/random anima tree injection; loaded fingerprint binds the reading.
Record current tuning separately: plant threshold 5 C; warm ticks 2; weather commonalities 60/15/15/10; fog accuracy 0.5 and range cap 22.9; these are source readings, not passing conditions.

Validate every public Mod Settings field default and serialization; next-version labels/off defaults; per-feature changed behavior, master/all-off, in-flight transition and restart roster scopes. Runtime def references and compiled source hash resolve.
Assert vrisk flight stats/whole-body frame references and observe FlightTracker; no unattended visual flight test. Source frame count is not a bar.

Record organic warm/ruin/wick/corpse generated-def injection and starting-charge application to generated and newborn stages; source-attributed explosion count catches duplicate krissek paths. Record the loaded wax safe-temperature limit and ingredient hazard during refinery work.

Reconcile ice mass and water outputs across ordinary bill, FlowWorks bucket/melter and passive melt; inventory reserve splits, merges, haul/unload and save/load. No cyclic recipe creates cold or mass.

Read fresh default map for absence of extra jobs/incidents/letters/drops/active carriers; keep defs/classes for references; enable each extra separately and observe its declared output; clean log in both arms.

Existing fake-game mutations and kernel fuzz are harness regression evidence only. Every result row needs source/assembly/data/settings/save fingerprint and real start/control/reset proof; unknown reads never become zero.
Compare natural versus scripted roster spawn/food/death/leave ledgers and full-map propagation graphs; record largest loss and stalled jobs without turning those tuning counts into passing bars.

Check shared/campaign consumers including RUT_BurnerAscendant, Watchers buried cues, ColdStorage seals and SWBestiary physiology for dangling types or unlabelled behavior; historical OWNER-cut soundscape/road/drip stay absent.

rules.rule: Water ice is inert water, mined by vanilla work. Mining speed/passion adds no local heat or probabilistic loot; containment acts on nearby living/dropped fuel.

Use existing plant Long-tick/vanilla flame explosion pathways; warm progress and warning/wick state survive save/load, split/merge and held-state transitions. Exactly one causal native fuel release per death; no arbitrary empty-cell jump.

Safe cutting/harvesting and sealed native ingestion do not fire the plant damage blast; foreign ingestion is visibly incompatible. All fresh native life stages acquire required physiology; butcher/corpse/food-processing transitions preserve organic hazards. Wax retains its hazard during refinery work until bill completion yields ordinary Chemfuel under the ratified life brief section 7 and R10.

No bespoke sun or heat kind. Vanilla room heat plus shared geometric Direct Sun applies; below-horizon sun on this nightside adds no invented local daylight. Loose water ice consumes finite sensible/latent reserve according to ambient exchange, never a chosen target thermostat or powered rack.

Owner card decision at BLUEDESERT_DESIGN_SITTING_1, recorded in the_blue_desert.md section 4b amendment: use Odyssey SandGrid for buildup/path-cost burial and erosion, with a local blue-white tint. Approach cells receive deposits and movement costs according to that engine. No windward special algorithm. Native fog handles accuracy/range/travel, ordinary rotation remains unlocked. Local ice-grain appearance changes no global sand material.

Ordinary wild growth, feeding and predation remain; no custom murrek top-up, minesweeping, storm-activated bloom or extra-generation loop. Shared ExplosiveGrowth must not convert ice into farm soil. Cleared connections may regrow naturally and must be inspected before each expedition.

Keep the existing roster and naming tiers: invented RM names stay RM, genuine canon patch remains external. Resolve local physiology compatibility without evicting a species or rewriting campaign history. Static abandoned works use generic material context; campaign epochs and study are off.

Existing vhaulk exit remains physical walking with readable notice; blocked/downed/tame animals are never silently removed, map teardown is not a voluntary departure, and death must remain a corpse/blast event. Shared native departures use CreatureBehaviors signs.

Defaults enable retained systems and disable every next-version extra. Major features have independent persistent switches, on/off timing labels, search and reset. Off retains saved identities; all-off stops scripted behavior without deleting beings. Existing optional states finish or neutralize according to tickets, never vanish silently.

Static site/mineable placement uses existing local content ownership on received maps. Ordinary Wreckage salvage and shared water-mass accounting remain. The cold-wax bill uses vanilla BiofuelRefinery and outputs ordinary vanilla Chemfuel, as specified by blue_desert_hydrocarbon_life.md section 7. Its cold-workspace operating condition keeps input stacks and the interaction cell at or below the loaded RM_ColdWax maxSafeTemperature, currently -1 C. The bill uses ordinary work with no custom temperature interlock. Wax retains its normal warning/ruin/wick state during work and interruptions. A warm workroom ruins or wicks the input before the bill finishes. Completed cold-room work yields ordinary fuel with vanilla stack merging, refueling and consumption behavior.

Warning state names its source, remaining response state and recovery action in inspect/readable notification; audio reinforces it but cannot be the sole warning. Immediate damage/EMP attacks are described hazards and need no artificial pre-impact delay. A warning alone never means survival while standing in a lethal blast.

meetings.why: One material/readability contract: distance hue does not license opaque blue plants or tan ground, while warning tells must remain locatable through the kept weather. State confirms identities; B1 supplies the only aesthetic judgment.

Water outputs share mass and residual-cold accounting. R10 fixes the wax bill to BiofuelRefinery. Wax retains its warm hazard through bill work, and cold-room completion yields ordinary vanilla Chemfuel under the ratified life brief section 7. T12/T13 and the situation generator must witness the input hazard and ordinary output use.

Leaving, dying, transporting and map teardown are different state changes. An eligible wild vhaulk physically walks; interruption waits/retries, tame/downed/blocked cases do not silently despawn. Notices explain a real exit, not a missing pawn.

Wild growth → grazing → predation death charges → blast loss → scarcity/respawn is a feedback loop. Fog travel and cleared gaps change encounter rates; paired trigger tests cannot establish seasonal survival.

Door traffic, room leakage, finite latent reserve, wax warm progress, weather and repair travel meet here. The loose-ice hold must persist far beyond an ordinary repair under its declared load. Current rack math establishes neither that comparison nor cold-workspace continuity.

Immediate damage/EMP cases and gradual warming cases are distinct transitions; an intact kinetic-killed cistern is a still-reactive cold corpse. Local removal of duplicate krissek death action does not remove the shared propane-lake class.

R2/R3/R9/R10/R11 preserve readable native identity and hazard debt across birth, death, organic stacks and containers, including wax during bill work. Cold-room refining yields ordinary Chemfuel under life brief section 7. State enumeration witnesses both the ingredient hazard and that output transition. Lifecycle implementation remains unproven.
Animal bodies and dropped/carried stacks can bridge apparently clear gaps; overlap of death blasts, flame heat and warning latency may eliminate useful preparation or ignite routine predation chains.

Containment is declared by reachable paths and causal fuel separation, not a fixed drawn gap. Storm deposits add path costs and colony doors affect access. Travel/thermal feasibility is explicitly unknown under heat/weather/propagation, so this argument claims only consistent semantics.

Ordinary physical context and normal jobs supply the same extraction opportunity. The deferred study, loot counter and timed emergence never appear as prerequisites; cold-cutting is specifically excluded by later owner answer.

The ruled SandGrid gives its thickest deposits a movement cost on approach cells beside structures. Engine evidence supplied in R1 establishes continued traversability and zero depth under full-fillage footprints. Whether natural storm traces reach that category beside representative walls, doors and hulls, and how that delay interacts with thermal repairs, still needs calibration. Post-storm or matched-weather reads isolate deposition from the storm movement multiplier.
